title: AI Regulation by Industry? OpenAI Proposes Common Limits
summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes common industry limits on AI models tracked by perplexity, and CEO Sam Altman backs the idea.
body_markdown:
Pachocki also gave a timeline. He wrote that "as soon as 2027 we could conceivably see a similar avalanche of fundamental pretraining advancements," with AI taking part in that research, and that AI-driven progress on alignment and monitoring is "unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining." As[Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/openai-scientist-proposes-industry-ai-limits-tied-to-model-intelligence-metric-5044174) summarized it, that could speed up progress faster than advances in monitoring and safety.


He listed the metric's weak spots too: labs use different evaluation datasets and training data, perplexity does not map directly to any single task, and it misses gains made outside pretraining, such as chain-of-thought reasoning.


## Anthropic (ANT): Amodei Called for Pacing in September


Pachocki described OpenAI's disclosure as "a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts," linking to[We Must Pace the Frontier](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier) , an essay Amodei published in September 2026. In it, Amodei wrote that "Frontier AI companies within democratic countries" should "coordinate to establish common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress."


Amodei went further on regulation. He wrote that "The most effective method of pacing is via regulation that targets all US frontier AI companies," and that some forms of coordination "will require government support," such as government mediation or waivers of antitrust restrictions. He said Anthropic is committing on its own to give third-party evaluators such as METR ongoing access to verify its safety practices, and called on governments to require other frontier companies to match. As reported by[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/) , Amodei's plan was seemingly endorsed by Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.


TechCrunch also noted that the filing for[Anthropic's IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-prices-83-raises-81-billion/) suggested the technology could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to society."


## Amazon (AMZN): 14.7% of Anthropic After Its IPO


According to[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/amazon-and-google-will-together-own-nearly-30-of-anthropic-after-its-ipo/) ,[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) was set to own 14.7% of Anthropic after its[initial public offering](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) , based on details Anthropic disclosed on November 17. Amazon invested in 2023 and 2024 through notes that convert into equity and kept billions of dollars of them unconverted; TechCrunch reported that converting all of them would lift its stake to 23.8%. Amazon's cloud unit AWS also stands to earn from Anthropic's commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.


## Alphabet (GOOGL): 13.7% of Anthropic via Google


[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) unit Google was set to hold 13.7% of Anthropic after the IPO, also in non-voting shares, per TechCrunch. Its stake comes from converted notes plus shares bought in a private placement, in which Google agreed to buy $10 billion worth of non-voting stock.
